subject: honeybee swarm
title: What If a Swarm of Bees Chased You?

scenes.text: What if a swarm of angry bees chased you? Jumping into water is the worst move.
Africanized honeybees attack in huge numbers and can chase you for more than a quarter mile.
They fly about 12 to 15 miles an hour. Most healthy people can outrun them.
A stinger left in your skin keeps pumping venom for up to a minute. Get it out within seconds.
An average adult can survive more than 1,100 stings. One man in 1962 survived 2,443.
But dive into a pond, and the bees just wait above the water until you come up for air.

description:
USDA bee researchers say Africanized bees defend in large numbers and may chase people more than a quarter mile; they fly about 12-15 mph, so run and cover your face, and do not jump into water because the bees wait for you to surface.
A stinger can keep injecting venom for up to a minute; the average adult can tolerate about 10 stings per pound of body weight. The Guinness record is 2,443 stings survived, in 1962.
